info.name: VectorText
info.comment: Extends the Vector class with support for generating text.

description.p: To create text along a path, set the Vector.GuidePath field with a reference to any Vector object that generates a path. The following extract illustrates the SVG equivalent of this feature:
description.pre:
<defs> <path id="myTextPath2" d="M75,20 l100,0 l100,30 q0,100 150,100"/> </defs>
<text x="10" y="100" stroke="#000000"> <textPath xlink:href="#myTextPath2"/> </text>
description.p: Support for bitmap fonts is included. This feature is implemented by drawing bitmap characters to an internal VectorImage and then rendering that to the viewport as a rectangular path. It is recommended that this feature is only used for fast 1:1 rendering without transforms. The user is otherwise better served through the use of scalable fonts.

Scalable fonts are laid out with unhinted glyph advances, which are fractional and are not rounded to the pixel grid. Hinting only affects the glyph outlines, so the width of a string scales linearly with its font size.

Scalable fonts are kerned by default, using the pair kerning that the font defines in its OpenType GPOS table, or in a legacy kern table. Kerning follows the font's variable instance, so a bold style can kern differently to a regular one. Like the advances, it is computed from font units without rounding, so it remains accurate when the text is scaled by transforms or viewBoxes. Kerning applies to every adjacent pair of characters within a line, including spaces, but not across line breaks. Set NO_KERNING in TextFlags to disable it, which is the equivalent of the SVG font-kerning property having a value of none. A font can also be excluded by setting Kerning = No in its section of fonts:options.cfg.

Only pair kerning is supported. Contextual kerning, ligatures, mark positioning and complex script shaping are not performed. Kerning lookups are taken from the font's Latin script definition if it has one, otherwise from its default script.

action.name: Clipboard
action.comment: Copies, cuts or pastes selected text through the system clipboard.

input.param: The mode that will be used to shift data between the target object and clipboard system.

description.p: CLIPMODE::COPY copies SelectedText as UTF-8. CLIPMODE::CUT copies the selection and removes it only after the clipboard accepts the text. Both operations leave the clipboard and text unchanged when nothing is selected or VTXF::SECRET is set in TextFlags.

CLIPMODE::PASTE replaces the selection, or inserts at the cursor when nothing is selected. CRLF and CR line endings are normalised to LF. With LineLimit set to 1, each line ending becomes a space. Other line limits reject a paste that would exceed the limit after replacing the selected rows. CharLimit truncates each resulting line in character columns, matching keyboard editing. Text after a null byte is ignored.
Cut and paste require VTXF::EDITABLE. Copy does not change the selection or call OnChange. Cut and paste call OnChange once if the text changes.

result.error: The operation completed, or there was nothing to copy or change.
The clipboard mode is not supported.
No text is available to paste.
The clipboard file is too large to read.
The Clipboard object could not be created.
The clipboard file could not be opened.
Cut or paste was requested for non-editable text.

input.param: The line number that you want to delete. If negative, the last line will be deleted.

description.p: This method deletes lines from a text object. You only need to specify the line number to have it deleted. If the line number does not exist, then the call will fail. The text graphic will be updated as a result of calling this method.

result.error: The Line value was out of the valid range.

method.name: GetCaretBounds
method.comment: Returns the line box at a character position.
method.prototype: ERR vt::GetCaretBounds(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Row, INT Column, DOUBLE * X, DOUBLE * Y, DOUBLE * Height)
method.tiriPrototype: err, X:num, Y:num, Height:num = GetCaretBounds(Row:num, Column:num)

input.param: Logical row, or a negative value for the current cursor row.
Character column, or a negative value for the current cursor column.
Receives the top of the line box.

description.p: Use GetCaretBounds to find where the caret sits at a given character position, for example to position a popup or scroll a container so that the cursor stays in view. The result describes a vertical line: X is the caret position, and Y and Height cover the line from the font's ascent to its descent.
Coordinates are in the parent viewport's coordinate space and include the scroll offset that keeps the cursor visible. Transforms applied to the VectorText are not included.
Out-of-range Row and Column values are clamped to the nearest valid position. A Column equal to the length of the line returns the position after the last character.
Caret geometry is only maintained when VTXF::EDITABLE or VTXF::SELECTABLE is set in TextFlags. The text layout is regenerated if necessary before the bounds are read.

result.error: Neither EDITABLE nor SELECTABLE is set in TextFlags, or no caret positions have been calculated.
The text follows a guide path.

method.name: SelectArea
method.prototype: ERR vt::SelectArea(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Row, INT Column, INT EndRow, INT EndColumn)

input.param: The line at which the selection starts.
The character column at which the selection starts.
The line at which the selection ends. If negative, the last line is used.
The character column at which the selection ends. If negative, the end of the line is used.

description.p: SelectArea() marks a region of text as selected, starting at the position given by Row and Column. The cursor is moved to the end of the region at EndRow and EndColumn, which may come before the start for a reversed selection. Columns are character positions, so UTF-8 sequences count as one column each. A negative EndRow refers to the last line and a negative EndColumn refers to the end of its line, so SelectArea(0, 0, -1, -1) selects all of the text. Positions beyond the text are clamped to its limits.

While an area is selected the AREA_SELECTED bit is set in TextFlags. For editable text, the next character typed, or a press of Backspace, Delete, Clear or Enter, will replace or delete the selected text. Moving the cursor without extending the selection deselects the area.

Text with VTXF::EDITABLE or VTXF::SELECTABLE displays the selected area with the SelectFill painter. The highlight is hidden when focus is lost and restored when focus returns; the selection range is retained.
If the start and end positions are identical, the cursor is moved and no area is selected.

field.name: Align
field.comment: Defines the alignment of the text string.

description.p: This field specifies the horizontal alignment of the text string. The standard alignment flags are supported in the form of ALIGN::LEFT, ALIGN::HORIZONTAL and ALIGN::RIGHT.
In addition, the SVG equivalent values of start, middle and end are supported and map directly to the formerly mentioned align flags.

field.name: CharLimit
field.comment: Limits the characters allowed on each logical line during editing.

description.p: CharLimit sets the maximum number of characters on each logical line, counted in UTF-8 characters rather than bytes. The limit applies to each line separately, not to the text as a whole. Use LineLimit to restrict the number of lines.

The limit applies to keyboard input and to pastes made through the Clipboard action. If an edit would exceed the limit, the line is cut off at the limit and any characters past that point are discarded. Deletions are always permitted.

Writing to the String field bypasses the limit, and reducing CharLimit does not shorten existing text. The default value is the maximum positive 32-bit integer, so there is effectively no limit. A value of 0 prevents any characters from being entered. Negative values are rejected with ERR::OutOfRange.

field.name: CursorColumn
field.comment: The current column position of the cursor.

field.name: CursorRow
field.comment: The current line position of the cursor.

field.name: DX
field.comment: Adjusts horizontal spacing on a per-character basis.

description.p: If a single value is provided, it represents the new relative X coordinate for the current text position for rendering the glyphs corresponding to the first character within this element or any of its descendants. The current text position is shifted along the x-axis of the current user coordinate system by the provided value before the first character's glyphs are rendered.

If a series of values is provided, then the values represent incremental shifts along the x-axis for the current text position before rendering the glyphs corresponding to the first n characters within this element or any of its descendants. Thus, before the glyphs are rendered corresponding to each character, the current text position resulting from drawing the glyphs for the previous character within the current ‘text’ element is shifted along the X axis of the current user coordinate system by length.

If more characters exist than values, then for each of these extra characters: (a) if an ancestor Text object specifies a relative X coordinate for the given character via a DX field, then the current text position is shifted along the x-axis of the current user coordinate system by that amount (nearest ancestor has precedence), else (b) no extra shift along the x-axis occurs.

field.name: DY
field.comment: Adjusts vertical spacing on a per-character basis.

description.p: This field follows the same rules described in DX.

field.name: Descent
field.comment: The font descent measured in pixels.

description.p: Use Descent to retrieve the height of the font descent region, which is the space reserved below the baseline. The value is measured in the same pixel units as FontSize, so it is unaffected by the display density and is subject to the same transforms as the text.

field.name: DisplayHeight
field.comment: The font height measured in pixels.

description.p: Use DisplayHeight to retrieve the height of the font, measured in the same pixel units as FontSize. For scalable fonts the value is the sum of the ascent and Descent. The value does not account for the display density or for transforms applied to the text.

field.name: DisplaySize
field.comment: The FontSize converted to points.

description.p: DisplaySize returns the FontSize converted from pixels to points at the fixed reference density of 96 DPI, calculated as FontSize * 72 / 96 and truncated to an integer. For example, a FontSize of 16 returns 12. The display density is not taken into account.
This value matches Point, except that Point is rounded to the nearest integer rather than truncated.

field.name: Face
field.comment: Defines the font face/family to use in rendering the text string.

description.p: The family name of the principal font for rendering text is specified here.

It is possible to list multiple fonts in CSV format in case the first-choice font is unavailable. For instance, Arial,Noto Sans would select the Noto Sans font if Arial was unavailable in the font database. The name of the closest matching font will be stored as the Face value.

field.name: Fill
field.comment: Defines the fill painter using SVG's IRI format.

description.p: The painter used for filling a vector path can be defined through this field using SVG compatible formatting. The string is parsed through the ReadPainter function. Please refer to it for further details on valid formatting.
Fallback colours and layered fill painters are supported in the same way as the Vector.Fill field. Please refer to it for further details.

field.name: Focus
field.comment: Refers to the object that will be monitored for user focussing.

description.p: A VectorText object with VTXF::EDITABLE or VTXF::SELECTABLE becomes active when its nearest viewport receives the focus. Setting the Focus field to a different vector in the scene graph redirects monitoring to it.
Changing this value post-initialisation has no effect.

field.name: Font
field.comment: Copies key meta information from a Font or other VectorText to create a matching text object.

description.p: To create a VectorText object that uses a matching typeset from another Font or VectorText object, set this field with a reference to that object. This can only be done prior to initialisation and the other object must have been initialised.

field.name: FontSize
field.comment: Defines the vertical size of the font.

description.p: The FontSize is equivalent to the SVG font-size attribute and refers to the height of the font from the dominant baseline to the hanging baseline. This would mean that a capitalised letter without accents should fill the entire vertical space defined by FontSize.

The default unit of FontSize is the pixel, and the value defines the em size of the font. A FontSize of 16 produces an em that is 16 pixels high in the text's coordinate space, which matches the behaviour of CSS and SVG. The display density is not applied, so the size on the display only changes if the text is transformed.

Standard unit measurements such as px, pt, pc, in, cm, mm and em are supported by appending them after the numeric value. Physical units are converted to pixels at a fixed reference density of 96 DPI, irrespective of the display, so 12pt is equivalent to 16px. Clients that need a physical size on a high density display must scale the value themselves, for example by multiplying a point size by DisplayDPI / 96. The em unit is fixed at 16 pixels. The final value is rounded to the nearest whole pixel, so 11pt (14.67px) becomes 15px. A size that rounds to less than one pixel is rejected with ERR::OutOfRange.
Reading FontSize returns the pixel size as a numeric string without a unit suffix.

NOTE: The FontSize is derived from information defined by the font author. Due to opinionated views on how font height is determined, the value is not transferrable between fonts. The primary difference is that some fonts will include the space for accents in the FontSize value, while others will not.

field.name: FontStyle
field.comment: Determines font styling.

description.p: The FontStyle selects a style from the font family. It can be a style name, a list of style descriptors, or a style name followed by descriptors. Descriptors are separated by ; and take the form key=value. Whitespace around each part is ignored. Examples:
description.pre: Bold Italic weight=Medium;width=ExtraCondensed Semi Bold;width=87.5% weight=550;slant=12;GRAD=-50 italic=yes;weight=Light
description.p: Conventional style names are Regular (the default), Bold, Italic and Bold Italic. Fonts can use any style name that the designer chooses, such as Thin or Condensed Bold; read fonts:fonts.cfg for the styles that are installed.
The following descriptors are supported. Keys and keywords are case-insensitive, and spaces, hyphens and underscores in keywords are ignored, so ExtraCondensed and extra-condensed are equivalent.

list.li: weight: A number from 1 to 1000, or a keyword: Thin or Hairline (100), ExtraLight or UltraLight (200), Light (300), Regular, Normal or Book (400), Medium (500), SemiBold or DemiBold (600), Bold (700), ExtraBold or UltraBold (800), Black or Heavy (900), ExtraBlack or UltraBlack (950). Sets the wght axis.

width: A percentage such as 75%, a plain number that is read as a percentage, or a keyword: UltraCondensed (50), ExtraCondensed (62.5), Condensed (75), SemiCondensed (87.5), Normal (100), SemiExpanded (112.5), Expanded (125), ExtraExpanded (150), UltraExpanded (200). Sets the wdth axis.
italic: yes, no, true, false, on, off, 1 or 0. Selects the italic file of the family, and sets the ital axis if the font has one.
slant: An oblique angle in degrees, where positive values lean to the right as in CSS. Sets the slnt axis to the negated value.
opsz: The optical size, which is a number, auto or none. The default, auto, sets the optical size to the font size in points. none uses the value of the named style or font default.

description.p: A four-character key that is a registered axis (wght, wdth, ital, slnt, opsz) or has no lower-case letters is an OpenType axis tag, e.g. GRAD=-50. Axis tags are case-sensitive. Other lower-case keys are reserved.

For variable fonts, the design coordinates are resolved in the following order, with later values taking precedence: the font defaults, the named style, the Weight field, the descriptors listed above, and finally axis tags. Values are clamped to the range of each axis, and axes that the font does not have are ignored. Strings that resolve to the same coordinates share the same cached font, so weight=Bold and Bold are equivalent.

For fonts that are not variable, the family's file that is the nearest match is chosen with the CSS font matching order of width, then italic, then weight. For instance, weight=SemiBold on a family that has no semi-bold file resolves to Bold. Axis tags are ignored and no synthetic styles are produced.

A complete font definition, as described for TextStyle, is also accepted. Only its style keys are used, and the face, size and paint keys have no effect. style=Semi Bold is an explicit spelling of a leading style name.
Errors are not returned if a style name or descriptor is invalid or unavailable. Invalid descriptors are reported as warnings in the log and otherwise ignored.

field.name: InlineSize
field.comment: Enables word-wrapping at a fixed area size.

description.p: The inline-size property allows the client to set the wrapping area to a rectangular shape. The computed value of the property sets the width of the rectangle for horizontal text and the height of the rectangle for vertical text. The other dimension (height for horizontal text, width for vertical text) is of infinite length. A value of zero (the default) disables the creation of a wrapping area.
By default, lines only break at whitespace and a word that is wider than the wrapping area will overflow it. Set WrapMode to allow lines to break within long words such as file paths and URLs.
The WrappedLines field reports the number of lines that are displayed after wrapping.

field.name: LetterSpacing
field.comment: Additional space between characters.

description.p: LetterSpacing adds a fixed distance between each pair of characters. A number is a distance in pixels and a scaled value is relative to FontSize, for example 2% is 2% of the font size and follows any change to it. Negative values bring the characters closer together. The default of zero adds no spacing.

No space is added after the last character of a line, and combining marks stay attached to their base character. TextWidth and word-wrapping both include the spacing. The field corresponds to the letterSpacing key of TextStyle, in which a scaled value is expressed with the em unit. It has no effect on bitmap fonts.

field.name: LineHeight
field.comment: Overrides the distance between the baselines of consecutive lines.

description.p: LineHeight replaces the font's natural line pitch. A number is a distance in pixels and a scaled value is relative to FontSize, for example 145% is 1.45 times the font size and follows any change to it. The default of zero uses the natural pitch of the font. Negative values are not permitted.
The pitch is rounded to a whole number of pixels and has a minimum of 1. The first baseline remains at Y, so the setting does not move the first line. LineSpacing reports the resulting pitch.
The field corresponds to the lineHeight key of TextStyle. Note that a number with no unit is a multiple of the font size in that key, so lineHeight=1.45 is equivalent to a field value of 145%.

field.name: LineLimit
field.comment: Restricts the total number of lines allowed in a text object.

description.p: Set the LineLimit field to restrict the maximum number of lines permitted in a text object. It is common to set this field to a value of 1 for input boxes that have a limited amount of space available.

field.name: LineSpacing
field.comment: The number of pixels from one line to the next.

description.p: This field can be queried for the vertical advance between each line of text, which reflects LineHeight if it is set. The value is measured in the same pixel units as FontSize, so it is unaffected by the display density and is subject to the same transforms as the text.

field.name: OnChange
field.comment: Receive notifications for changes to the text string.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to receive notifications whenever the text string changes.
The callback function prototype is void Function(*VectorText).

field.name: OnCursorMove
field.comment: Receives notifications after cursor or selection changes.

description.p: Set this field with a function reference to be notified when the cursor position, selected area or text content changes. This is commonly used to update status displays or to keep the cursor in view with GetCaretBounds.

An operation that moves the cursor or selection more than once triggers a single notification, which reports the final state. When the text changes, OnChange is called first. Text layout is regenerated before the callback runs, so caret geometry and cursor fields are up to date. Cursor or selection changes made from inside the callback do not trigger another notification.
Notifications are only sent after initialisation, and only when VTXF::EDITABLE or VTXF::SELECTABLE is set in TextFlags.
The callback function prototype is void Function(*VectorText).

field.name: Point
field.comment: Returns the point-size of the font.

description.p: Reading the Point value will return the point-size of the font, calculated as FontSize * 72 / 96 and rounded to the nearest integer. The conversion uses the fixed reference density of 96 DPI that applies to all FontSize units, not the density of the display.

field.name: Rotate
field.comment: Applies vertical spacing on a per-character basis.

description.p: Applies supplemental rotation about the current text position for all of the glyphs in the text string.

If multiple values are provided, then the first number represents the supplemental rotation for the glyphs corresponding to the first character within this element or any of its descendants, the second number represents the supplemental rotation for the glyphs that correspond to the second character, and so on.
If more numbers are provided than there are characters, then the extra numbers will be ignored.
If more characters are provided than numbers, then for each of these extra characters the rotation value specified by the last number must be used.

If the attribute is not specified and if an ancestor 'text' or 'tspan' element specifies a supplemental rotation for a given character via a 'rotate' attribute, then the given supplemental rotation is applied to the given character (nearest ancestor has precedence). If there are more characters than numbers specified in the ancestor's 'rotate' attribute, then for each of these extra characters the rotation value specified by the last number must be used.

This supplemental rotation has no impact on the rules by which current text position is modified as glyphs get rendered and is supplemental to any rotation due to text on a path and to 'glyph-orientation-horizontal' or 'glyph-orientation-vertical'.

field.name: SelectColumn
field.comment: Indicates the column position of a selection's beginning.

description.p: If the user has selected an area of text, the starting column of that area will be indicated by this field. If an area has not been selected, the value of the SelectColumn field is undefined.
To check whether or not an area has been selected, test the AREA_SELECTED bit in the TextFlags field.

field.name: SelectFill
field.comment: The painter used to highlight selected editable text.

description.p: Accepts the same colours, paint servers and layered painters as Vector.Fill. The default is rgba(0,120,215,0.35). The highlight is drawn over the glyphs, so a translucent painter keeps them legible. Selection highlights follow the text's transforms and are hidden while focus is lost.

field.name: SelectRow
field.comment: Indicates the line position of a selection's beginning.

description.p: If the user has selected an area of text, the starting row of that area will be indicated by this field. If an area has not been selected, the value of the SelectRow field is undefined.
To check whether or not an area has been selected, test the AREA_SELECTED bit in the TextFlags field.

field.name: SelectedText
field.comment: The selected text, with line breaks separating selected lines.

description.p: Returns an empty string when there is no selection or the SECRET flag is set in TextFlags.

field.name: ShapeInside
field.comment: Reference a vector shape to define a content area that enables word-wrapping.

description.p: This property enables word-wrapping in which the text will conform to the path of a Vector shape. Internally this is achieved by rendering the vector path as a mask and then fitting the text within the mask without crossing its boundaries.
This feature is computationally expensive and the use of InlineSize is preferred if the text can be wrapped to a rectangular area.

field.name: ShapeSubtract
field.comment: Excludes a portion of the content area from the wrapping area.

description.p: This property can be used in conjunction with ShapeInside to further restrict the content area that is available for word-wrapping. It has no effect if ShapeInside is undefined.

field.name: String
field.comment: The string to use for drawing the glyphs is defined here.

description.p: The string for drawing the glyphs is defined here in UTF-8 format. Lines are separated by line feeds.

The retrieved string contains every line of the text, separated by line feeds, including any changes made by the user while editing. Line breaks introduced by word-wrapping (see InlineSize) are not included.

field.name: TextFlags
field.comment: Controls text presentation, editing and selection.

field.name: TextLength
field.comment: The expected length of the text after all computations have been taken into account.

description.p: The purpose of this attribute is to allow exact alignment of the text graphic in the computed result. If the computed text width does not match this value, then the text will be scaled to match the TextLength.

field.name: TextStyle
field.comment: A portable font definition that describes the complete appearance of the text.

description.p: TextStyle reads and writes the whole font selection as a single string, for instance face=Noto Sans; size=15px; weight=650; fill=#1d2433; shadow=3px 4px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.4). The keys are listed in the Font Definitions manual, and NormaliseTextStyle can be used to validate them. The field can be set before or after initialisation.

Assignment overwrites the declared keys only, and an empty string has no effect. Style keys update individually, so italic=yes retains an earlier weight=650. An absent fill or stroke leaves the existing value unchanged and stroke=none clears the stroke. If the string contains a malformed value then ERR::Syntax is returned and the settings are unchanged.

The shadow, glow and blend keys are rendered through a VectorFilter that belongs to the text, which replaces the value of #Filter while any of them is active. blend requires a backdrop, which is provided by setting the ISOLATED flag on an enclosing viewport. The features key, a kerning value of optical, and any strokeAlign other than centre, are stored and returned but are not rendered at present.

Reading the field returns the canonical form of the current state, including changes that have been made through fields such as Face and FontSize. The result can be assigned to another VectorText or saved.

field.name: TextWidth
field.comment: The pixel width of the widest line in the String field.

description.p: This field will return the pixel width of the widest line in the String field. The result is not modified by transforms. Kerning is included unless NO_KERNING is set in TextFlags. For scalable fonts the width is fractional and is not rounded, so it can be used to position adjacent text exactly. Round the value up if a whole pixel width that contains the text is required.

field.name: TotalLines
field.comment: The total number of lines stored in the object.

field.name: Weight
field.comment: Defines the level of boldness in the text.

description.p: The Weight is equivalent to the CSS font-weight value, ranging from 1 to 1000. The default of 400 renders text in its normal state. Lower values such as 300 render light text, while higher values such as 700 render bold text.

For variable fonts, the Weight sets the wght axis and takes precedence over the weight of a named FontStyle. A weight descriptor in the FontStyle takes precedence over the Weight. For other fonts, the Weight is used to choose the nearest matching file of the family.
A Weight of 400 is treated as unset, and therefore cannot reset the weight of a named style such as Bold.

field.name: WordSpacing
field.comment: Additional space at the end of each word.

description.p: WordSpacing adds a fixed distance to each space (U+0020) and non-breaking space (U+00A0). A number is a distance in pixels and a scaled value is relative to FontSize, for example 25% is a quarter of the font size and follows any change to it. The value can be negative. The default of zero adds no spacing.

TextWidth and word-wrapping both include the spacing. The field corresponds to the wordSpacing key of TextStyle, in which a scaled value is expressed with the em unit. It has no effect on bitmap fonts.

field.name: WrapMode
field.comment: Controls where word-wrapping may break a line.

description.p: WrapMode determines where a line may be broken when InlineSize enables word-wrapping. It has no effect if InlineSize is zero.
The default, WORD, only breaks lines at whitespace. A word that is wider than the wrapping area stays on a line of its own and overflows it.
In SYMBOL mode, a word is also divided into segments after each of the following symbols, and a line may break between any two segments:

types.type: File and URL paths, e.g. /usr/ share/ kotuku
URL queries, e.g. page? id= 4& x= 2

description.p: A break after a symbol is suppressed if the symbol is the last character of the word, or the next character is also a break symbol (so // and -- are never split). A - does not permit a break if it is part of the hyphens that start a word, as in --log-warning, or if it is followed by a digit, as in x-1. Periods, commas, colons and semi-colons are not break symbols, so numbers such as 3.14, times and file extensions are kept whole. The symbol always remains at the end of the earlier line and no hyphen is inserted at the break.

ANYWHERE mode extends SYMBOL by breaking between characters when a segment is too wide to fit on a line of its own, so that no line overflows the wrapping area. A segment is only divided in this way when it cannot fit on an empty line. At least one character is always placed on each line, so a glyph that is wider than the wrapping area will overflow it. Breaks are made between UTF-8 characters, but combining marks are not treated specially and can be separated from the character that they modify.

Text with the SECRET flag in TextFlags is always wrapped in WORD mode, so that the line breaks do not reveal the positions of symbols in the hidden string. Text that follows a guide path is not wrapped.

field.name: WrappedLines
field.comment: The total number of lines after word-wrapping is applied.

description.p: WrappedLines reports the number of lines that are displayed by the text, including the additional lines created when InlineSize wraps a line of the String. If word-wrapping is disabled, the value is the same as TotalLines.
Reading this field will update the text layout if it is out of date, which can be expensive for large blocks of text.

field.name: X
field.comment: The x coordinate of the text.

description.p: The x-axis coordinate of the text is specified here as a fixed value. Scaled coordinates are not supported.

field.name: Y
field.comment: The base-line y coordinate of the text.

description.p: The Y-axis coordinate of the text is specified here as a fixed value. Scaled coordinates are not supported.
Unlike other vector shapes, the Y coordinate positions the text from its base line rather than the top of the shape.

constants.comment: Universal values for alignment of graphics and text
constants.const: Align to bottom
Synonym for HORIZONTAL | VERTICAL
Align to horizontal center
Align to left
Synonym for HORIZONTAL | VERTICAL
Align to right
Align to top
Align to vertical center

constants.comment: VectorText wrapping modes, used when InlineSize is set.
constants.const: As for SYMBOL, and a segment that is too wide for a line of its own is broken between characters.
As for WORD, and lines may also break after the symbols listed in the WrapMode documentation, such as the / in a file path.
Lines break at whitespace only. A word that is wider than the wrapping area overflows it. This is the default.
Automatically set if a region of text has been selected.
Enable animated blinking (not supported - exists as SVG dummy option).
Allow user editing and selection of the text if the nearest viewport has the focus. Implies SELECTABLE.
Allow user editing and selection of the text if the nearest viewport has the focus. Implies SELECTABLE.
Enable a strike-through line in the text.
Leave text scrolling to its container; disables automatic cursor offsets.
Disable the pair kerning defined by the font. Equivalent to setting the CSS font-kerning property to none.
Disables support for system-keys that enable common key combinations such as Ctrl-C, Ctrl-X etc.
